analyzed_vuln.description: `audio_sample_entry_box_read` can delete `ptr->esd` via `gf_isom_box_del_parent(&ptr->child_boxes, (GF_Box*)ptr->esd)` in its fallback ESDS-scanning path, but it does not reliably clear all ownership/containment references before later cleanup. The same ESDS box pointer remains reachable through parent child-box lists and is freed again during recursive `gf_isom_box_del`/`gf_isom_box_array_del`, causing a heap-use-after-free in `gf_isom_box_del` when it dereferences an already-freed box.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: In `fuzz_parse`, a crafted `mp4a` sample entry with malformed/odd nested data triggers `gf_isom_box_array_read` failure and enters the fallback scan in `audio_sample_entry_box_read` (around line 4044+). If an `esds` child was already parsed/registered, the code deletes it early with `gf_isom_box_del_parent`, then reparses/re-adds state inconsistently. On movie teardown (`gf_isom_delete_movie`), recursive box-list deletion visits the stale ESDS reference again, leading to UAF/double-delete behavior (`esds_box_del` free first, later `gf_isom_box_del` read on freed object).
